elements.evidence: its contractors acting on Client's behalf

elements.element: Transferable to a successor in an M&A transaction
elements.evidence: successor in interest by merger, acquisition or sale of all or substantially all of the assigning party's assets

offending_extra_words: or sale of all or substantially all of the assigning party's assets
reasons: The locked target was preferred, but the redline delivers only the affiliate/contractor extension and successor transferability; it says nothing about paid-up licences being perpetual and irrevocable, and nothing limiting revocation/termination of subscription licences to uncured material breach. Preferred is therefore incomplete.

Both fallback elements are satisfied on their material terms: affiliates are covered (indeed without the notice condition, which is more favourable to us) and transfer to an M&A successor is expressly permitted without consent. The clause as redlined sits at the fallback.

Minimality gate fails: operation 1 expands 12 words to 21 and operation 2 expands 15 words to 36 (ratios 1.75 and 2.40). The successor carve-out could be tightened (e.g. 'or to a successor in interest by merger or sale of substantially all assets') rather than the long tri-part formulation.

Intent is preserved: the non-exclusive scope, the ordinary-course field of use, the Client's freedom to use alternative systems, and the mutual consent requirement for other assignments all remain effective; no undefined terms are introduced. Minor drafting nit: 'in the ordinary course of its business' now follows three grantees, so 'its' is slightly ambiguous and could read 'their respective businesses'.
